items.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025

ctx.x: Whoever wrote this promo on your website spoke about them saying, "They also had a brilliant ability to figure out what the people wanted to hear. The result? The sound of Philadelphia." How did they figure out what people wanted to hear?

Well I used to say they had the pulse. They had the beat and pulse of the neighborhoods if that makes sense. In a way it's like jazz. You know they had the beat and pulse of the neighborhoods. So to me that — my phrase that they knew what people wanted to hear, that's what I mean. And also I think if you go back and pick song to song there was a lot of like how do you say this, there was a lot of over—emotional songs that Gamble used to write. He was quite a hell of a lyricist. And some of those songs, "Me and…
